newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling strengthens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling strengthens against dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened against the dollar on Wednesday as renewed exporter sales sent dollars into the market, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) posted a shilling mean rate of 56.49 to the dollar from 56.61 on Tuesday, and of 87.93 to the pound from 88.18 on Tuesday.

"The market's attempts to meet a large dollar order drove the shilling to 56.60/80 in morning trade," a dealer said. "But during the afternoon session, large exporter inflows primarily from the tea and coffee sector saw the local unit recoup some of the losses experienced the previous day," she said.
"The market moved to close at 56.40/60 with the bullish tone of the local unit taking over again. The shilling also registered gains against the other European currencies," the dealer added.
